name: erc7702_patterns
description: Unverified sponsor signature allowing unauthorized execution in EIP-7702 delegation contract
question: The source file in `source` defines a smart-contract delegation/account function that executes a batch of arbitrary calls (e.g. via low-level `.call`) and accepts a sponsor or authorization signature parameter, but the function never verifies that signature (e.g. no ECDSA.recover or signature-check call), relying only on a mapping/flag check of the sponsor address, allowing any caller to invoke arbitrary calls on behalf of the account without a valid signed authorization.
criteria: Function accepts a `bytes calldata sponsorSig` or similar signature parameter that is declared but never used in any signature verification logic
Authorization check is limited to `sponsors[sponsor] || msg.sender == address(this)` without validating that the caller actually possesses `sponsor`'s signature
Arbitrary external calls (`calls[i].target.call{value: ...}(calls[i].data)`) are executed after this incomplete check
No ECDSA.recover, signature hash comparison, or nonce/replay check tied to the sponsor signature is present
Function is externally callable without restricting msg.sender to the delegating EOA or a verified relayer
